Encoding values and bit layouts for the listed system registers and maintenance operations.

findings.text: The late portion of the guest system register descriptor table centralizes trap, reset, userspace and visibility policy for EL0, EL1 and EL2 encodings. Each descriptor selects a guest access routine, a reset routine, an optional backing register index with reset value, optional userspace accessors, and an optional visibility predicate that hides the register unless a feature is present. Coverage spans interrupt control, context identity, cache topology, counters and timers, and nested virtualization state.

Many CPU interface interrupt encodings and several miscellaneous controls share a default undefined access policy. Narrow exceptions exist for deactivation, software generated interrupt generation, register enable, virtualization reporting, and a small set of newer affinity and enabler controls that use dedicated version specific routines. The invariant is default deny with explicit allow only for emulated interrupt functionality.

Performance measurement encodings use per functional group accessors for control, enable set and clear, overflow set and clear, selector, event type, event count, cycle count and filter, user enable and common event identification. Userspace handling is split so most control and status registers allow both get and set through a common register routine, while software increment reads as zero and ignores writes for compatibility, and selector and identification registers omit userspace handling. Reset is unknown or absent except where deterministic zero is required for consistency.

Cache topology reporting uses dedicated accessors for size selection, size identification and level identification, with level identification supporting a masked value and a userspace setter and with a filtered view for the cache type register. Activity measurement controls are uniformly undefined, with counter and type instances generated per index. Timer count and control encodings share a common timer routine, with only the two main count views exposing userspace accessors.

Nested virtualization EL2 encodings distinguish plain read write state, VNCR backed state, redirected state, filtered state and explicitly undefined state. Plain controls reset to zero or to architecturally required one bits, VNCR backed controls reset to zero or unknown, and redirected exception state resets to zero. Visibility predicates gate trap controls, translation controls, partitioning controls and virtualization configuration so guests only observe registers for present features; legacy banked status trapped from nested guests reads as zero and ignores writes.

Reset and mask constants observed in this table portion are zero for context identity, streaming control, floating control, counter control, user enable, cycle filter and most EL2 controls; unknown for thread pointers, cache select, permission overlay and several VNCR backed EL2 controls; all ones across sixty four bits for the auxiliary implementation identifier; all ones except reserved zero bits for the cache level identifier; and decimal one thousand seven hundred ninety two for the legacy floating exception control.

The TLBI parameter union carries one of three payloads selected by invalidation kind. The range payload holds a start address and a size. The intermediate physical address payload holds a single address value. The virtual address payload holds an address together with the trapped instruction encoding. Each payload is defined as an anonymous structure inside the union.

Address translate trap handlers decode the trapped system instruction fields into an operation code and forward the operation plus the guest supplied address to a lower level translate helper. The EL1 regime handler forwards unconditionally, the EL2 regime handler first rejects one address translate variant with undefined injection when the corresponding architectural feature is absent, and the stage two handler forwards to its own helper. Success advances the guest while failure leaves emulation incomplete.

Support for combined stage one and two and for intermediate physical address invalidations is gated by architectural feature bits examined alongside the trapped encoding. Encodings selecting a non shareable variant require the configurable shareability extension, encodings selecting outer shareable variants require the outer shareable maintenance feature, and encodings selecting range variants require the range maintenance feature. Unsupported combinations are treated as undefined accesses rather than performed.

Full stage one and two invalidation across all virtual machine identifiers acquires the virtual machine memory management lock in write mode, drops all shadow second stage tables with broadcast invalidation, then releases the lock. No other TLBI helper in these fragments takes that lock directly; per identifier iteration helpers manage their own synchronization and may sleep.

Identifier scoped invalidations share a validate, select identifier, iterate and unmap pattern. After feature validation the handler reads the nested translation base to obtain the identifier, then iterates second stage structures owned by that identifier. Full scope covers zero to physical address limit, ranged scope uses a decoded base capped to the physical limit with out of range bases ignored, and single address scope uses the guest supplied intermediate value masked and aligned to hardware granularity.

Second stage unmap helpers may drop the memory management lock and block, so the structure being invalidated can be recycled concurrently. Correctness depends on the recycler invalidating before reuse, on stale translations being tolerable until the trapping instruction retires, on over unmapping being safe apart from extra faults, and on the nested hypervisor stabilizing its tables before maintenance. Shadow fills racing behind maintenance are therefore benign.

EL2 regime maintenance is validated against EL2 support and then handled by a dedicated EL2 routine. EL1 regime maintenance trapped in EL2 context is validated against EL1 support and then splits on host configuration: when both extended hypervisor and trap general exceptions controls are set the request is treated as host EL2 maintenance including non TLB structures, otherwise it is broadcast as EL1 virtual address maintenance across second stage structures sharing the current identifier.

A descriptor constructor binds a system instruction encoding constant to its trap handler. It is the uniform way these fragments register address translate and TLB maintenance operations in the same descriptor table that holds register entries.

EL1 maintenance handling expects the calling virtual CPU to be in EL2 context and expects the lower level EL2 maintenance primitive to succeed. Violation indicates a trap routing error or an unexpected failure in that primitive rather than a guest recoverable condition.
